newsitem.title: USA: LADWP recommends 3-yr agreement with Duke-Dreyfus.
newsitem.headline: LADWP recommends 3-yr agreement with Duke-Dreyfus.

text.p: The staff of the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power (LADWP) recommended Tuesday the municipal utility sign a three-year agreement with Duke-Louis Dreyfus for wholesale trading and retail products and services.

LADWP earlier Tuesday said it selected Duke-Louis Dreyfus, a joint venture of North Carolina utility Duke Power Co and Louis Dreyfus Natural Gas Corp, as a strategic partner to meet the challenges of a deregulated power market.
The agreement must be approved by the LADWP board and reviewed by the City Council. It was still unclear when the recommendation would be sent to the City Council for aproval.
William McCarley, LADWP general manager, said the utility needs to improve its financial position by increasing revenue and reducing its $7.9 billion debt.
By taking full advantage of market opportunities in the area of wholesale trading, the utility hopes to increase its revenue, McCarley said in a statement.

Offering new products and servcies will help retain at-risk customers, or those likely to chose another power supplier when this choice becomes available in California in January 1998, and will also provide additional sources of revenue, he added.
"The agreement guarantees LADWP a minimum of $6 million (in revenue) the first year from the alliance," the statement said.

Duke-Louis Dreyfus will benefit only if LADWP's business grows and increases its revenue and Louis Dreyfus will be responsible for any trading losses, a key condition of the agreement designed to protect customers.
The strategic alliance is the first of several the utility will likely enter into in coming years.

The LADWP board on Tuesday is also expected to consider a recommendation by McCarley that a task force be convened to develop a process to evaluate the feasability of a strategic alliance on the regulated side of the electric utility business.

Edison International, the parent company of rival utility Southern California Edison, is seeking to reopen the bidding process that led to Duke-Louis Dreyfus winning LADWP's recommendation as its strategic partner.
LADWP is the nation's largest municipal utility, serving a city population of more than 3.5 million, with annual revenue of $1.9 billion.
